explanation: When a line is given as a table of (x, y) pairs, the slope is the change in y divided by the change in x between any two rows. The sliders build the table from a steady rule: each row steps x by Δx and y climbs by m·Δx. Watch the highlight sweep from row to row -- the green Δx and violet Δy change rows but their ratio (the slope) stays exactly the same, which is what makes the table linear.
bullets: Slope = Δy / Δx between any two rows of the table.
In a linear table every equal step in x gives the SAME step in y.
Pick any pair of rows -- the slope you compute is identical.
